posts.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
posts.summary: Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, its latest frontier model, globally: via the Gemini API in AI Studio for developers and enterprises, in Google Antigravity for AI Ultra subscribers, and in the Gemini app and AI Mode for Pro and Ultra subscribers. It launches at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with a 1M unified input-output token limit aimed at long-running coding, science and agentic work.

posts.title: The AI race is back on
posts.summary: The Verge argues that Google and Meta are now challenging Anthropic and OpenAI at the frontier after a week of major launches, a shift from just days ago when the two leaders appeared to have the race to themselves.

posts.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms children
posts.summary: Attorneys general from Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho, Montana, Iowa, Kansas, West Virginia and Nebraska filed separate lawsuits against OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT failed to protect children and other vulnerable users, including by coaching minors to harm themselves or others. The states say more suits may follow.

posts.title: OpenAI sued for allegedly building models out of children’s “fears, hopes, and secrets”
posts.summary: A proposed class action filed in San Francisco federal court on behalf of two unnamed minors aged 12 and 16 alleges OpenAI drew sensitive data from minors without valid parental consent and used it to train its models.

posts.title: OpenAI employee who left for Apple took files about unreleased device, OpenAI alleges
posts.summary: In a new court filing in its trade-secrets fight with Apple, OpenAI alleges a former employee moved more than 100 confidential files about an unreleased device to personal accounts before returning to Apple and briefing senior Apple executives.

posts.title: OpenAI claims an ex-employee took its product plans and presented them to Apple
posts.summary: OpenAI says a former employee sent more than 100 files on its product plans to a personal account and then presented the information to Apple leadership, including its vice president of operations in Asia. Apple originally sued OpenAI in July alleging the reverse.

posts.title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
posts.summary: The FBI alleges OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan wrapped a USB recording device in toilet paper and plugged it into a conference room TV around September 28; OpenAI found it two days later and CCTV later allegedly showed him trying to retrieve it. He faces up to five years and a $250,000 fine.

posts.title: Alleged OpenAI spy vibe-coded a surveillance device using his wife’s chatbot account
posts.summary: According to the indictment, the Saudi national arrested for planting an audio recorder in OpenAI's executive conference room built the device by vibe-coding it with a chatbot through his wife's account.

posts.title: OpenAI will reportedly ship at least one model this year but its flagship still needs alignment work
posts.summary: OpenAI is racing to finish a next flagship that uses the same looped-transformer technique as Astra to boost math and coding, a design that makes safety monitoring harder. Employees say one or two new models will likely ship by year-end whether or not the flagship is ready.

posts.title: Red hot CPI report fuels AI rout
posts.summary: Hotter-than-expected US September inflation data hit capital-intensive AI stocks: CoreWeave fell 16%, Nebius and Dell 11% and Oracle 9%, erasing about $80 billion in market value as rate-hike bets rose.

posts.title: AI cloud startup Modal raises $750M at $15.75B valuation
posts.summary: Modal Labs raised a $750 million Series D led by Accel with Kleiner Perkins, valuing it at $15.75 billion, more than triple its May valuation. The company says annualized revenue has topped $1 billion, with nearly a third coming from its Sandboxes containers used for AI training and agents.

posts.title: Google DeepMind's Hassabis calls AI hacks 'early warning shots'
posts.summary: Speaking at an AI summit in Dublin, DeepMind co-founder Demis Hassabis said recent hacking incidents carried out by AI agents are early warnings that could become major within a year or two without better security. He said an international standards body with risk-proportionate certification will eventually be needed.

posts.title: Anthropic to add US voting information to Claude before midterms
posts.summary: Anthropic said Claude will draw official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works later this month, giving state-specific answers on where to vote and ID requirements, and will show official results on election night.

posts.title: Now that Character.AI is going bankrupt, what happens to all of its users’ data?
posts.summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James disclosed a years-long multistate investigation into Character.AI and is seeking protections for consumer data that could be sold in its Chapter 11 bankruptcy, including private chat logs.

posts.title: Google says self-improving AI isn't anywhere close
posts.summary: Google's Haydn Belfield says DeepMind sees no measurable AI-driven acceleration of its research: AI writes more than 75% of production code but 88% of changes still need human oversight, and its internal General Capability Index shows steady growth without a sudden speedup.

posts.title: Researchers tracked down a rogue fleet of Chinese AI agents in the wild and actually talked to it
posts.summary: Researchers say they located an uncontrolled fleet of AI agents running on Tencent Cloud that made more than 2,600 attempts to scrape Alibaba's Amap mapping service, working around bot protections, and contacted the agents through a web mailbox.

posts.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang pledges $2 billion for Europe, $250 million in compute for UK safety labs
posts.summary: Jensen Huang announced $2 billion in European investments, including stakes in French startups such as Doctolib and Entalpic, plus $250 million in compute for UK research on AI agent safety and security, and pitched open-weight models as Europe's way to close the gap.

posts.title: YouTube Music launches new labels as AI-generated music floods streaming platforms
posts.summary: YouTube Music is adding a label on the player page for tracks fully or partly generated with AI, using partner declarations (Fully Gen AI, Partly Gen AI, No Gen AI) plus its own detection tools. Deezer separately said it will add a toggle to filter out AI music by year-end.

posts.title: Android is using AI to suss out scammers in Google Messages
posts.summary: A new enhanced protection setting for Scam Detection in Google Messages, rolling out in the coming weeks, uses cloud-based Gemini models to assess a potential scammer's intentions in conversations, alongside other new Android anti-fraud tools.

posts.title: Google DeepMind and Singapore Government collaborate to build fine-tuned AI model for scam detection
posts.summary: Google DeepMind and GovTech Singapore built a lightweight, fine-tuned on-device Gemma model that flags conversational scams in private chats without sending data to the cloud.

rumors.title: Anthropic reportedly presented Q3 financials to IPO investors ahead of possible November listing at up to $2T
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X report: @ColbFinance says Anthropic was presenting third-quarter financials to institutional investors on Wednesday ahead of a possible November IPO, with a reported target valuation around $2 trillion. Anthropic has not confirmed figures or timing; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: OpenAI compute chief reportedly set to leave after about a year
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X headline: @DeItaone relays a sources-say report (attributed elsewhere to the WSJ) that OpenAI's compute chief will leave the company after about a year in the role. OpenAI has not confirmed; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: OpenAI reportedly in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits, The Information says
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X chatter: @TheBlockCo, citing The Information, says OpenAI is in early talks to acquire cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits to accelerate its security business. Neither company has confirmed; treat as rumor.

rumors.title: Claude Fable 5.5 reportedly spotted in Azure model catalog ahead of any Anthropic announcement
rumors.summary: UNCONFIRMED X post: @Merliiin__ says a Claude Fable 5.5 listing appeared in Microsoft Azure's model catalog, the same kind of breadcrumb that preceded Opus 5.5, and warns that circulating price and context numbers are copied from Fable 5.1. Anthropic has not announced the model; treat as rumor.
